Equality and dignity at work

Approval and review history

This handbook was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 April 2023, this version took effect 1 July 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in July 2027.

Why the wellbeing and benefits summary was added

A review found a new starter often did not discover the discount scheme or long service recognition scheme until well into their employment, simply because these were documented separately and not consistently introduced during induction; consolidating a summary directly into this handbook ensures every new starter sees the full picture of what Alderbridge offers from their very first day, alongside the more formal contractual terms.

Uniform and dress code

Training and development

Health and safety responsibilities

Uniform and appearance

Whistleblowing

Ending employment

Why the wellbeing and benefits summary was added

A staff survey found that many employees were not fully aware of the wellbeing support already available to them, since information was spread across several separate policies each covering only one aspect; this version's consolidated summary, mirroring the same addition made to the Employee Handbook and Terms document, addresses that gap directly.

Probationary period

A new employee typically serves a probationary period set out in their own contract, during which their performance and suitability for the role is assessed through regular informal check-ins with their registered manager; successful completion is confirmed in writing.

Performance management summary

Alderbridge expects every employee to perform their role to a good standard; a performance concern is normally addressed informally in the first instance through supportive conversation and, where needed, a short improvement plan.

Employee recognition

Alderbridge recognises good work through a variety of means, including a simple thank-you from a manager, a mention in a team meeting, or a nomination for an annual staff recognition award.

Travel between sites

An employee occasionally required to travel between Alderbridge sites as part of their role claims travel expenses per the Expenses Policy, and any time spent travelling between sites during a working day is counted as working time.

Social media

An employee is personally responsible for what they post on social media; a post that identifies Alderbridge, a resident, or a colleague is subject to the same standards of conduct and confidentiality that apply at work.

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time
employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on the same basis.

2. Submit a leave request via the rota system at least 14 days before the requested dates for a non-peak
period, or at least 28 days before the requested dates over the Christmas and New Year period.

3. The registered manager reviews the request against minimum safe staffing levels and other
already-approved leave, approving wherever practicable and explaining clearly where a request cannot be
accommodated as submitted.

4. Up to 5 days of unused leave may be carried into the next leave year with the registered manager's
written agreement, used within the first three months of the new leave year or forfeited.

5. Leave already approved is not withdrawn except in a genuine, significant operational emergency, and
any such withdrawal is discussed directly with the affected employee rather than simply cancelled without
explanation.

6. Where an employee is sick during a period of approved annual leave, the affected days are recorded as
sickness rather than annual leave, and the leave is returned to their entitlement to use another time.

Exceptions and professional judgement

A shorter-notice request may still be granted where staffing allows and the reason is genuinely
time-sensitive (for example, an unexpected family event), assessed by the registered manager on the
specific circumstances rather than automatically declined for falling outside the standard notice period.

Governance and reporting

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

Investigating fairly

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

Health and safety responsibilities

Grievance and dispute resolution

Training and development

Uniform and appearance

Workplace Pension Scheme: What You Need to Know

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the workplace pension scheme available to Alderbridge staff. It applies to every eligible employee across every site.

Policy statement

Alderbridge automatically enrols an eligible staff member into the workplace pension scheme, meeting its legal auto-enrolment duty while making it straightforward for a staff member to understand their own options.

Definitions

**Auto-enrolment** the legal requirement to enrol an eligible staff member into a pension scheme automatically. **Opt-out** a staff member's choice to leave the scheme after being enrolled, which they may do at any time. **Salary sacrifice** an alternative contribution method some staff may choose, reducing gross salary in exchange for an equivalent pension contribution.

1. Automatically enrol every eligible staff member into the pension scheme from their qualifying start date.
2. Provide clear information about contribution rates and the opt-out process at enrolment.
3. Process an opt-out request within the statutory window, refunding any contribution already deducted where the opt-out is timely.
4. Re-enrol an opted-out staff member automatically every three years, as required by law, unless they choose to opt out again.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Benefits Guidance (the wider set of benefits this scheme sits alongside) and payroll's own processing calendar for contribution deductions.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the opt-out window. A new staff member is auto-enrolled on their start date, and decides within the first month that they would prefer to opt out for now. Payroll processes this within the statutory window and refunds the single contribution already deducted, and the staff member is told they will be automatically re-enrolled in three years unless they opt out again at that point.

Salary sacrifice option

Closing note

A workplace pension is a meaningful long-term benefit, and this guidance exists to make sure every staff member understands their own choices about it clearly from day one.

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time
employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on the same basis.

Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handover Procedure (governing the practical handover of their duties) and the Grievance Procedure (a separate route for a staff member who wishes to raise a formal concern rather than share informal exit feedback).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

Purpose and scope

This handbook sets out the core terms and conditions of employment applying to every Alderbridge Care Group employee, given to every new starter and available for reference at any time.

Hours of work

A full-time role is contracted at 37.5 hours per week, with a part-time role's hours set out in the individual contract.

Flexible working

A staff member may request a flexible working arrangement per the Flexible Working Policy.

Your place in the organisation

Alderbridge is organised into three regions (North West, Midlands, South West), each led by a regional manager overseeing the sites within that region, reporting through Central Support Office to the Chief Executive.

Pay and pay reviews

Pay is reviewed annually, with any increase communicated in writing and reflected in the following month's pay run.

Annual leave

Annual leave entitlement follows the Annual Leave Policy, starting at 28 days inclusive of bank holidays for a full-time role.

Overtime and time off in lieu

Overtime is paid per the Overtime Payment Guidance, with a time off in lieu election available as an alternative.

Wellbeing and benefits summary

Beyond core pay and leave, Alderbridge offers a retail discount scheme, a long service recognition scheme marking a 5, 10, 15 and 20-year milestone, and staff wellbeing guidance and support; this section is new in this version, consolidating what was previously scattered across several separate documents into one accessible summary within the handbook a new starter reads on their very first day.

Sickness absence

A staff member reports a sickness absence to their line manager before their shift start time.

Pension

Every eligible staff member is automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme per the Pension Scheme Guidance.

Probationary Period Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out the probationary period every new employee serves, and how it is reviewed and confirmed. It applies to every new starter, and to any existing employee moving into a new role that Alderbridge treats as requiring a fresh probationary assessment.

Policy statement

Probation is a genuine, two-way assessment period: Alderbridge assesses whether the new starter is settling well and meeting the role's requirements, and the new starter assesses whether the role and Alderbridge are right for them, with support and honest feedback flowing in both directions throughout.

Definitions

**Probationary period** the standard 6-month period from an employee's start date during which suitability is formally assessed. **Extension** an additional period, up to 3 months, added where more time is genuinely needed to reach a fair decision. **Probation review** a scheduled formal conversation reviewing progress against the role's requirements.

Roles and responsibilities

**The line manager** holds regular informal check-ins and every formal review, raising any concern as soon as it arises rather than saving it for a scheduled review. **HR** confirms the outcome of each formal review in writing and advises on any complex case. **The new starter** engages openly with feedback and raises any concern about their own induction or support.

The probationary period runs for 6 months from the start date, extendable by up to a further 3 months at the registered manager's discretion where more time is needed.

Formal review meetings are held at 6 weeks, 3 months and 5 months, each recorded in writing.

Any conduct, capability or attendance concern is raised with the employee as soon as it arises, not held back until the next scheduled review.

Successful completion of probation is confirmed to the employee in writing, normally by the end of the 6-month period.

Disciplinary Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group deals fairly with conduct and performance concerns, informed by, but not a copy of, the Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures. It applies to every employee, from their first day of employment, though the specific right to bring an unfair dismissal claim depends on separately applicable statutory qualifying service.

Definitions

**Misconduct** a failure to meet the standards of conduct expected, addressed through the staged process below. **Gross misconduct** conduct serious enough to justify dismissal without notice following a fair process, examples of which are given later in this procedure. **Capability** a genuine inability to meet the required standard despite reasonable support, which may follow this same staged process or, where appropriate, a separate capability process focused on support rather than sanction.

Roles and responsibilities

**The line manager** normally handles informal action and may chair a first-stage formal hearing. **HR** advises at every formal stage, ensures consistency across sites, and must be involved before any final written warning or dismissal is confirmed. **A manager not previously involved in the matter** hears any appeal, at a level senior to whoever made the original decision.

Informal action

Minor conduct or performance concerns should wherever possible be resolved informally through a supportive conversation between the employee and their line manager, recorded in a brief dated note kept on the employee's personal file. Informal action is not a disciplinary sanction and does not itself entitle the employee to be accompanied, though a manager may agree to this as good practice where asked.

Where informal action has not resolved the concern, or the matter is sufficiently serious to bypass the informal stage, an investigation is carried out by a manager not otherwise involved, gathering statements and any relevant evidence.

Where the investigation finds a case to answer, the employee is invited in writing to a formal hearing, given at least 2 working days' notice, told the specific allegation, and provided with the investigation evidence in advance.

The employee has the right to be accompanied at the hearing by a trade union representative or a work colleague of their choice.

At the hearing, the employee is given a full opportunity to respond to the allegation, ask questions, and present their own evidence before any decision is reached.

A decision is confirmed in writing within 5 working days of the hearing wherever possible, giving reasons and, where a sanction is applied, its duration and the right of appeal.

The first formal stage is normally a first written warning, live for 6 months; a further offence within that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, may move directly to a final written warning, live for 12 months.

A further offence while a final written warning is live may result in dismissal with notice, or without notice if the conduct amounts to gross misconduct.

An employee may appeal any formal outcome in writing within 10 working days, to a manager not previously involved, whose decision is final within Alderbridge's own internal process.

Gross misconduct examples

Examples of gross misconduct include theft, physical violence, being under the influence of drugs or alcohol on duty, gross negligence causing serious harm to a person supported, serious breach of the Safe Administration of Medication Policy or Controlled Drugs Procedure, and serious or repeated breach of confidentiality. This is not an exhaustive list; the Employee Handbook's Section 4 gives further illustrative examples, and a matter not listed here may still be treated as gross misconduct where its seriousness genuinely warrants it.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where an allegation also raises a safeguarding concern, the Safeguarding Adults Policy and Allegations Against Staff Procedure run in parallel with this procedure; a decision to suspend on full pay pending investigation is taken on safeguarding grounds and is never treated as itself a disciplinary sanction or a presumption of guilt.

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time
employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on the same basis.

The employee has the right to be accompanied at the hearing by a trade union representative or a work colleague of their choice.

At the hearing, the employee is given a full opportunity to respond to the allegation, ask questions, and present their own evidence before any decision is reached.

A decision is confirmed in writing within 5 working days of the hearing wherever possible, giving reasons and, where a sanction is applied, its duration and the right of appeal.

Gross misconduct examples

Examples of gross misconduct include theft, physical violence, being under the influence of drugs or alcohol on duty, gross negligence causing serious harm to a person supported, serious breach of the Safe Administration of Medication Policy or Controlled Drugs Procedure, and serious or repeated breach of confidentiality. This is not an exhaustive list; the Employee Handbook's Section 4 gives further illustrative examples, and a matter not listed here may still be treated as gross misconduct where its seriousness genuinely warrants it.

Local and regional variations

Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handover Procedure (governing the practical handover of their duties) and the Grievance Procedure (a separate route for a staff member who wishes to raise a formal concern rather than share informal exit feedback).

Definitions

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Issue a key or access card to a permanent staff member from their first day; the previous 4-week qualifying period has been removed.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Return all keys and access cards to the registered manager on an employee's last working day, before their final pay is released; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

Policy statement

allow faster status checks between renewals — this is now a requirement, not an option — supporting both
regulatory compliance and administrative efficiency.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the detailed criminal record and barring check required for a role involving
regulated activity with a vulnerable adult. **DBS Update Service** the subscription service allowing a DBS
certificate's status to be checked online rather than a fresh application, saving time on onward checks,

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time
employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on the same basis.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Gross misconduct examples

Governance and reporting

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

Investigating fairly

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

This policy exists to hold both of those truths at once: genuine support for a genuinely unwell employee, and a fair, transparent process where a pattern needs to be understood and, where necessary, addressed.

Definitions

**Self-certification** an employee's own written statement confirming the reason for absence, valid for the first 7 calendar days of any absence. **Fit note** a certificate from a GP or other authorised healthcare professional required for any absence beyond 7 calendar days, stating whether the employee is 'not fit for work' or 'may be fit for work' with modified duties. **Trigger point** a defined threshold of absence occasions or days that prompts a specific management response, set out in the table below. **Return-to-work discussion** the short, supportive conversation held with every employee on their first day back from any absence, regardless of its length. **Disability-related absence** absence wholly attributable to a condition meeting the Equality Act 2010's definition of disability, which is treated differently for trigger-point purposes as explained below.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** reports their own absence personally wherever possible, provides certification as required, and engages constructively with any return-to-work discussion or, where a pattern has triggered one, a formal absence review. **The line manager or registered manager** receives the initial report, arranges cover, holds the return-to-work discussion, and escalates a triggered pattern promptly rather than letting it accumulate unaddressed. **HR** advises on trigger-point application, coordinates any occupational health referral, and ensures the policy is applied consistently across every site rather than varying by how strictly an individual manager happens to interpret it. **Occupational health**, where referred, provides an independent clinical view on fitness for work and any reasonable adjustment that might help an employee return sooner or more sustainably.

Report your absence by telephone to your line manager, or the on-call manager out of hours, no later than one hour before your shift is due to start — a text message or a message relayed through a colleague is not acceptable except where you are medically incapable of making a call yourself, in which case a family member may call on your behalf.

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time

Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.

Governance and reporting

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

Investigating fairly

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

Definitions

Roles and responsibilities

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

Worked example

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

Where the investigation finds a case to answer, the employee is invited in writing to a formal hearing, given at least 2 working days' notice, told the specific allegation, and provided with the investigation evidence in advance.

The employee has the right to be accompanied at the hearing by a trade union representative or a work colleague of their choice.

At the hearing, the employee is given a full opportunity to respond to the allegation, ask questions, and present their own evidence before any decision is reached.

A decision is confirmed in writing within 5 working days of the hearing wherever possible, giving reasons and, where a sanction is applied, its duration and the right of appeal.

The first formal stage is normally a first written warning, live for 6 months; a further offence within that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, may move directly to a final written warning, live for 12 months.

A further offence while a final written warning is live may result in dismissal with notice, or without notice if the conduct amounts to gross misconduct.

An employee may appeal any formal outcome in writing within 10 working days, to a manager not previously involved, whose decision is final within Alderbridge's own internal process.

Gross misconduct examples

Examples of gross misconduct include theft, physical violence, being under the influence of drugs or alcohol on duty, gross negligence causing serious harm to a person supported, serious breach of the Safe Administration of Medication Policy or Controlled Drugs Procedure, and serious or repeated breach of confidentiality. This is not an exhaustive list; the Employee Handbook's Section 4 gives further illustrative examples, and a matter not listed here may still be treated as gross misconduct where its seriousness genuinely warrants it.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where an allegation also raises a safeguarding concern, the Safeguarding Adults Policy and Allegations Against Staff Procedure run in parallel with this procedure; a decision to suspend on full pay pending investigation is taken on safeguarding grounds and is never treated as itself a disciplinary sanction or a presumption of guilt.

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies to this procedure — disciplinary process is deliberately standardised across all five sites and Central Support Office to ensure consistent, fair treatment regardless of location.

Governance and reporting

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

Investigating fairly

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Sickness Absence Policy (which governs the boundary between sickness
and leave), the Family and Parental Leave Policy (governing a separate category of leave), and the
Overtime Procedure and Payroll Calendar (which records how leave affects pay calculation).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates fair handling of a peak-period conflict. Three staff at Riverside House all
request the same week off over Christmas. The registered manager reviews the requests against the order
they were submitted and each employee's leave taken so far that year, approves two of the three, and
discusses the third directly, offering an alternative week close to the original request, rather than declining
outright with no further conversation.

Frequently asked questions

**What happens to unused leave if I leave Alderbridge partway through the leave year?** Any accrued but
unused leave is paid in your final salary, calculated pro-rata to your leaving date. **Can I take a single day
of annual leave, or does it need to be a full week?** A single day is entirely acceptable, subject to the
same notice period. **Does a bank holiday I don't work on count against my entitlement?** No — bank
holidays are included within the 28-day entitlement rather than added on top, so working or not working a
specific bank holiday does not change your overall entitlement, only how it is used.

Training and competency

Registered managers receive guidance on fair leave management as part of their wider
people-management training, including how to balance competing requests transparently.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews leave-taking patterns across sites annually to identify anyone who is not taking their full
entitlement, since under-taken leave is itself a wellbeing concern worth a supportive conversation, not
simply a convenient staffing outcome.

Record keeping and retention

Leave records are retained per the Records Retention Schedule, held alongside the wider personnel file.

Workplace Pension Scheme: What You Need to Know

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the workplace pension scheme available to Alderbridge staff. It applies to every eligible employee across every site.

Policy statement

Alderbridge automatically enrols an eligible staff member into the workplace pension scheme, meeting its legal auto-enrolment duty while making it straightforward for a staff member to understand their own options.

Definitions

**Auto-enrolment** the legal requirement to enrol an eligible staff member into a pension scheme automatically. **Opt-out** a staff member's choice to leave the scheme after being enrolled, which they may do at any time. **Salary sacrifice** an alternative contribution method some staff may choose, reducing gross salary in exchange for an equivalent pension contribution.

1. Automatically enrol every eligible staff member into the pension scheme from their qualifying start date.
2. Provide clear information about contribution rates and the opt-out process at enrolment.
3. Process an opt-out request within the statutory window, refunding any contribution already deducted where the opt-out is timely.
4. Re-enrol an opted-out staff member automatically every three years, as required by law, unless they choose to opt out again.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Benefits Guidance (the wider set of benefits this scheme sits alongside) and payroll's own processing calendar for contribution deductions.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the opt-out window. A new staff member is auto-enrolled on their start date, and decides within the first month that they would prefer to opt out for now. Payroll processes this within the statutory window and refunds the single contribution already deducted, and the staff member is told they will be automatically re-enrolled in three years unless they opt out again at that point.

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Extends the PIN-release requirement to scan-to-email, and adds a mandatory data wipe step for a printer or scanner reaching end of life.*

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains safe use of a printer and scanner at an Alderbridge site. It applies to every staff member using shared print and scan equipment.

Policy statement

A document containing resident data is printed using secure PIN release, and scan-to-email now also requires PIN authentication before sending, a new extension introduced in this version, with a printer or scanner reaching end of life now requiring a mandatory data wipe.

Definitions

**Shared printer or scanner** equipment used by multiple staff. **Secure PIN release** the mandatory printing method requiring a personal PIN before a document prints. **Scan-to-email PIN authentication** the new requirement, introduced in this version, extending PIN authentication to the scan-to-email function. **End-of-life data wipe** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, wiping a printer or scanner's internal storage before disposal or return.

1. Print any document containing resident data using secure PIN release.
2. Authenticate with your PIN before using the scan-to-email function; this is a new requirement introduced in this version, extending the previous print-only PIN control.
3. Scan a document to the correct, intended recipient only, double-checking the destination before sending.
4. Shred a printed draft or misprint containing resident data.
5. IT completes a data wipe of a printer or scanner's internal storage before it is disposed of, returned to a leasing company, or repurposed; this is a new mandatory step introduced in this version.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Data Protection and Information Governance Policy, the Password and Account Access Guidance, and the Data Encryption Standard (relevant to the end-of-life wipe's technical approach).

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 6 months after an employee leaves (shortened from the previous 2-year
period), then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Purpose and scope

It applies to every employee at every site.

Welcome and organisational overview

Alderbridge Care Group operates a small number of residential and nursing care homes, each led by its own registered manager, organised into regions each led by a regional manager, supported by organisation-level functions: Human Resources, the Health and Safety Lead, the Safeguarding Lead, and the Chief Executive's office.

Understanding the regional management structure

Each site's registered manager reports to a regional manager, who oversees several sites within a defined geographic area and coordinates activity, such as emergency mutual aid and multi-agency safeguarding support, across those sites.

Employment basics

Every employee receives a written contract setting out their specific role, hours, and pay; this handbook explains the general terms that apply across Alderbridge and points to the specific policy governing a particular topic in more detail.

Frequently asked questions

**Does a hospital appointment count as sickness absence?** No — a pre-arranged medical appointment is treated as authorised time off under a separate, informal arrangement with your line manager, not recorded against your sickness absence trigger points, provided reasonable notice is given. **What if I'm off sick on a day I was due to take annual leave?** The day is recorded as sickness, not annual leave, and the annual leave day is returned to your entitlement to use another time. **Can my manager contact me while I'm off sick?** Only for a genuine welfare check-in at a frequency you have agreed together, never to ask when you'll be back in a way that feels like pressure to return before you are ready. **What happens at the end of a sustained absence if I'm not able to return to my previous role at all?** HR and occupational health explore every reasonable adjustment and alternative role first; ill-health capability dismissal is considered only as a genuine last resort, following its own fair process, once all reasonable options have been properly explored and exhausted.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

Enhanced DBS checks are renewed every 3 years, and staff must register with the DBS Update Service to
allow faster status checks between renewals — this is now a requirement, not an option — supporting both
regulatory compliance and administrative efficiency.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the detailed criminal record and barring check required for a role involving
regulated activity with a vulnerable adult. **DBS Update Service** the subscription service allowing a DBS
certificate's status to be checked online rather than a fresh application, saving time on onward checks,
registration with which is now mandatory. **Renewal cycle** the 3-year interval at which a full check is
renewed.

Roles and responsibilities

registered manager 8 weeks before expiry. **The registered manager** ensures the renewal application is
submitted in good time and confirms DBS Update Service registration for every staff member requiring an
enhanced check. **The staff member** completes the renewal application promptly when asked and must
register with the DBS Update Service.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

Investigating fairly

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Extended frequently asked questions

**Can I refuse to work alone at all, in any circumstance?** Raise any general concern about lone working with your manager; while some degree of lone working is a genuine feature of the community support role, a specific, well-founded concern about your own capacity to work safely alone is taken seriously and discussed individually rather than dismissed as simply part of the job. **What if the mobile app itself fails or is unreliable in a specific area with poor signal?** Report this to the office immediately so a fallback (a scheduled telephone check-in instead) can be arranged for visits in that area, rather than the app's own unreliability becoming an unaddressed safety gap. **Does the office know my real-time location during a visit, not just at check-in?** The app records check-in and check-out location and time; it is not a continuous real-time tracker, reflecting a deliberate balance between safety monitoring and a client's own privacy in their home.

Weather and seasonal community-visiting risk

During severe weather, the Willow Bank registered manager assesses whether scheduled visits can proceed safely, prioritising clients with the most critical needs (for example, a medication round) if any visits genuinely need to be postponed, and communicating any change to affected clients and their families directly rather than a worker simply failing to arrive without explanation; lone workers are never expected to attempt a visit their own professional judgement, or an explicit management instruction, considers unsafe given the conditions.

Reviewing the lone working model itself

Beyond reviewing individual incidents, the Alderbridge Health and Safety Lead reviews the overall lone working model — the check-in interval, the welfare-call and escalation timings, and the mobile app's own reliability — at least annually, incorporating any near miss or genuine incident from the preceding year, so the model itself evolves based on real operational experience rather than remaining fixed indefinitely from when it was first introduced.

Annual Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how annual leave is calculated, requested and approved across Alderbridge Care
Group, including the leave year, carry-over rules, and notice periods for requesting leave. It applies to
every employee, full-time and part-time, from their first day of employment.

Policy statement

Rest and recovery time is treated as essential to sustaining good care over the long term, not a
discretionary benefit; this policy is designed to make leave genuinely straightforward to request and take,
while being honest about the real staffing constraints a 24-hour care environment operates under.

Definitions

**Leave year** the 12-month period, 1 April to 31 March, against which annual leave entitlement and
usage is measured. **Pro-rata entitlement** the proportionally reduced entitlement calculated for a
part-time employee based on their contracted hours relative to full-time. **Carried-over leave** unused
leave from one leave year moved into the next under the specific conditions this policy allows. **Peak
period** the Christmas and New Year period, during which a longer notice period applies to leave requests
given typically higher demand.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** submits leave requests via the rota system within the notice periods this policy sets out.
**The registered manager** approves or declines requests, balancing fair access to leave against
maintaining safe staffing levels, and communicates a decision within a reasonable time so employees can
plan. **HR** tracks entitlement and carry-over centrally and advises on any complex calculation (for
example, for an employee who changed hours partway through the leave year).

1. Full-time employees receive 28 days' annual leave per leave year, inclusive of bank holidays; part-time
employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated on the same basis.

International adoption and additional leave considerations

Where an adoption involves a child from overseas, additional adoption leave provisions account for the travel and in-country matching period specific to that process, coordinated closely between the employee and HR given the less predictable timeline such arrangements can involve compared to a domestic adoption match.

Pay during family leave in detail

Statutory maternity, paternity and adoption pay is calculated per current legislation and administered by payroll, with Alderbridge's own contractual enhancement, where one applies to a specific role or length of service, explained clearly to the employee alongside the statutory calculation so the two are never confused with one another, and any query about the specific figures is directed to payroll rather than estimated informally by a line manager.

Returning to a different site or shift pattern

An employee returning from an extended period of family leave may request to return to a different site or shift pattern where their personal circumstances have changed; this is considered genuinely and fairly alongside any operational constraint, following the same principles as an ordinary flexible working request under the Flexible Working Policy, rather than automatically defaulting to exactly the previous arrangement regardless of whether it still suits the employee.

Supporting a phased and flexible return

Where an employee wishes to combine their return from family leave with a flexible working request (for example, reduced hours or a compressed week), the two conversations are held together wherever practicable, so the employee experiences one coordinated planning discussion with HR and their line manager rather than two separate, disconnected processes covering closely related ground.

Miscarriage and early pregnancy loss

An employee experiencing a miscarriage before 24 weeks is supported compassionately, with any resulting absence recorded sensitively and separately from ordinary sickness absence trigger-point calculations, recognising the particular nature of this loss regardless of the exact statutory categorisation that applies to the time off itself.

Renewal workflow

Preparation starts far enough ahead to gather the current care plan, capacity assessment, restrictions and evidence of less restrictive alternatives. An approaching expiry without acknowledgement, a changed restriction or a condition that cannot be met is escalated to the registered manager and governance lead. a fair opportunity to give their own account before the investigation concludes, and the outcome — whether the complaint is upheld, partially upheld, or not upheld — is communicated to that staff member directly, separately from the response sent to the complainant, so the two communications can each be pitched appropriately to their different audience and purpose.

Withdrawing a complaint partway through investigation

A complainant may withdraw a complaint at any point; where the concern raised also touches on a safeguarding or serious incident matter, that separate process continues regardless of the complaint being withdrawn, since a complainant's own decision about pursuing their individual complaint does not determine whether an underlying safety concern still needs investigating in its own right.

Recording a complaint the complainant asks not to be formally investigated

Occasionally someone raises a concern verbally but explicitly asks that it not be treated as a formal complaint or investigated further; their wishes are respected regarding formal investigation, but the substance of what was raised is still logged on the site's own informal concerns record so that, if a similar theme emerges from another source later, the pattern is still visible to the registered manager rather than each individual soft concern disappearing without trace.

Complaints raised via social media or a public review site

Where a concern is raised publicly rather than through Alderbridge's own channels, the registered manager responds courteously and briefly in public, inviting the person to make contact directly so the matter can be looked into properly and given the same thorough response any other complaint would receive, rather than attempting to resolve the substance of a detailed care concern in a public comment thread, where doing so risks both an inadequate response and an inappropriate disclosure of personal information about the situation.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Issue a key or access card to a permanent staff member from their first day; the previous 4-week qualifying period has been removed.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Return all keys and access cards to the registered manager on an employee's last working day, before their final pay is released; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

Email Retention Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Retention period shortened from 2 years to 6 months to
reduce data protection risk.

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 6 months after an employee leaves (shortened from the previous 2-year
period), then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Retention and disposal

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.
Automatic deletion is suspended for a legal hold, investigation, subject-access search or other authorised
preservation requirement. When the hold ends, disposal resumes under the relevant schedule and is
recorded where the record class requires evidence of destruction.

Access and assurance

Managers arrange controlled mailbox access for absence, leavers or investigations through the
documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

Following any fall, do not move the resident until a basic check for obvious injury has been completed, unless leaving them in place presents its own risk.

Contact the on-call registered manager immediately after any fall, regardless of whether an injury is apparent.

Where injury is suspected, also contact the falls lead immediately, in addition to the on-call registered manager; this dual-contact requirement is new in this version and was not required previously.

Call emergency services immediately for a suspected serious injury, such as a suspected fracture or head injury with loss of consciousness, regardless of falls lead availability.

Record every fall, including one without apparent injury, in the resident's care record and the site's falls log, noting whether the falls lead was contacted.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where the falls lead is not immediately reachable following a suspected-injury fall, the on-call registered manager proceeds with emergency services contact where warranted without waiting, and the falls lead is updated as soon as they become available, since the new dual-contact step is additive and never delays an emergency response.

Local and regional variations

Harbour View's higher proportion of residents with complex mobility needs means it holds a dedicated falls prevention equipment store, including a range of mobility aids not routinely stocked at smaller sites, and its falls lead role is filled by a permanent on-site physiotherapist given the site's larger nursing capacity.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a fall also triggers) and the CQC Notification Procedure (governing when a fall meets the notifiable serious injury threshold).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the new dual-contact standard. A resident is found on the floor of their room during a night shift, with a suspected wrist injury visible on the basic check. The care assistant contacts both the on-call registered manager and the falls lead, as this version now requires for a suspected-injury fall, and the falls lead's clinical input helps determine that a GP review rather than an emergency department visit is the appropriate next step.

outright with no further conversation.

same notice period. **Does a bank holiday I don't work on count against my entitlement?** No — bank
holidays are included within the 28-day entitlement rather than added on top, so working or not working a
specific bank holiday does not change your overall entitlement, only how it is used.

Family and Parental Leave Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental and parental bereavement leave at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every employee meeting the relevant statutory eligibility criteria for each specific type of leave.

Policy statement

Alderbridge supports employees through significant family events with clarity and compassion, administering statutory entitlements accurately while ensuring every conversation about family leave feels supportive rather than transactional.

Definitions

**Ordinary maternity leave** the first 26 weeks of maternity leave. **Additional maternity leave** the further 26 weeks available after ordinary maternity leave. **Shared parental leave** leave that may be shared between parents following a birth or adoption, subject to eligibility. **Keeping in touch day** an optional, paid day an employee on family leave may work without ending their leave.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** notifies HR as early as practicable of their intention to take family leave, per the statutory notice requirements. **HR** confirms eligibility, entitlement and pay, and coordinates the practical return-to-work planning. **The line manager** maintains reasonable contact during leave, agreed with the employee, and plans cover for the absence.
