Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handover Procedure (governing the practical handover of their duties) and the Grievance Procedure (a separate route for a staff member who wishes to raise a formal concern rather than share informal exit feedback).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

A staff member with a workplace concern uses the Grievance Procedure for a personal employment matter, or the Whistleblowing Policy where the concern relates to a wider wrongdoing or risk, including an anonymous route where preferred.

Safeguarding responsibilities

Every staff member, regardless of role, has a personal responsibility to recognise and report a safeguarding concern immediately per the Adult Safeguarding Policy and the wider safeguarding suite, a responsibility that sits above any other single term of employment given what is genuinely at stake for a resident.

Leave and absence

Annual leave entitlement is set out in each employee's own contract and requested through the standard leave request process; sickness absence is reported to the registered manager as early as possible on the first day of absence, now with a wellbeing check-in offered as part of the return-to-work process.

Standards of conduct

Every employee is expected to treat a resident, colleague, and visitor with dignity and respect at all times, to act within the boundaries of their own training and competence, and to raise a concern honestly rather than conceal it.

Health and safety responsibilities

Every employee has a personal responsibility to work safely, to report a hazard or near-miss promptly, and to follow the specific safety procedure relevant to their role; the Health and Safety Policy (Full Manual) sets out the complete framework.

Safeguarding responsibilities

Every employee has a personal responsibility to report a safeguarding concern immediately to their registered manager, following the Adult Safeguarding Policy.

Equality, diversity and inclusion

Alderbridge is committed to treating every employee and resident fairly regardless of a protected characteristic; a concern about discrimination or unfair treatment is raised with Human Resources and taken seriously.

Confidentiality and data protection

An employee has access to confidential information about a resident, a colleague, or Alderbridge's own business in the course of their role; this information is shared only on a need-to-know basis and never disclosed outside of work.

Use of Alderbridge equipment and systems

Alderbridge equipment is provided for legitimate work purposes; reasonable personal use of a shared computer is generally acceptable where it does not interfere with work or breach confidentiality.

Grievance and dispute resolution

Where an employee has a concern about their treatment at work, they are encouraged to raise it informally with their registered manager in the first instance; where this does not resolve the matter, the formal Grievance Procedure sets out the full process.

Every employee completes mandatory training relevant to their role as part of induction and on an ongoing refresher basis; a development conversation takes place at least annually as part of the appraisal process.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Issue a key or access card to a permanent staff member from their first day; the previous 4-week qualifying period has been removed.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Return all keys and access cards to the registered manager on an employee's last working day, before their final pay is released; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

Email Retention Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Retention period shortened from 2 years to 6 months to
reduce data protection risk.

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 6 months after an employee leaves (shortened from the previous 2-year
period), then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Retention and disposal

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.
Automatic deletion is suspended for a legal hold, investigation, subject-access search or other authorised
preservation requirement. When the hold ends, disposal resumes under the relevant schedule and is
recorded where the record class requires evidence of destruction.

Access and assurance

Managers arrange controlled mailbox access for absence, leavers or investigations through the
documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.

Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handover Procedure (governing the practical handover of their duties) and the Grievance Procedure (a separate route for a staff member who wishes to raise a formal concern rather than share informal exit feedback).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.

documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

This procedure works alongside the Contractor Management Policy (governing a contractor's separate, temporary access arrangement) and the Exit Interview Guidance (part of the same final-week leaver process this return requirement now sits within).

A worked example illustrates both changes together. A new care assistant now receives their own key on their very first day rather than waiting 4 weeks as under the previous version. Exit Interview Guidance for Line Managers

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how Alderbridge Care Group conducts an exit interview with a departing staff member. It applies to every voluntary resignation across every site.

Policy statement

An exit interview gives a departing staff member a genuine, confidential opportunity to share honest feedback, helping Alderbridge understand and act on the real reasons people choose to leave.

Definitions

**Exit interview** the voluntary conversation offered to a departing staff member, usually in their final week. **Themed feedback** anonymised, aggregated feedback from multiple exit interviews, reported to HR without attributing a specific comment to a named individual.

1. Offer every departing staff member an exit interview, making clear it is voluntary and can be declined without any consequence.
2. Conduct the interview with someone other than the staff member's own direct line manager, to support open, honest feedback.
3. Keep individual responses confidential, feeding only themed, anonymised patterns back to HR and site leadership.
4. Complete the interview in the staff member's final week, at a time that suits them.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handover Procedure (governing the practical handover of their duties) and the Grievance Procedure (a separate route for a staff member who wishes to raise a formal concern rather than share informal exit feedback).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates confidentiality in practice. A departing staff member mentions in their exit interview a specific colleague's approach they found difficult. This individual comment is not passed on directly; instead, if a similar theme emerges across several exit interviews at the same site, it is reported to leadership as an anonymised pattern worth investigating.

Sickness absence

A staff member reports a sickness absence to their line manager before their shift start time.

Pension

Every eligible staff member is automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme per the Pension Scheme Guidance.

Notice periods table

Length of service	Notice period (either party)
During probationary period	1 week
Up to 2 years	1 week per completed year, minimum 1 week
2 years or more	1 week per completed year, up to a statutory maximum

Disciplinary and grievance

A concern about a staff member's conduct or performance is handled per the Disciplinary Procedure, and a staff member's own concern is handled per the Grievance Procedure.

Equality and dignity at work

Alderbridge is committed to equality of opportunity and a workplace free from discrimination, harassment or bullying, per the Equality, Dignity and Respect at Work Policy.

Confidentiality

A staff member handles resident and organisational information confidentially at all times.

Approval and review history

This handbook was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 April 2023, this version took effect 1 July 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in July 2027.

Why the wellbeing and benefits summary was added

A review found a new starter often did not discover the discount scheme or long service recognition scheme until well into their employment, simply because these were documented separately and not consistently introduced during induction; consolidating a summary directly into this handbook ensures every new starter sees the full picture of what Alderbridge offers from their very first day, alongside the more formal contractual terms.

Uniform and dress code

A uniformed role wears the provided uniform per the Dress and Appearance Guidance, and a non-uniformed role dresses in professional, business-casual attire.

Training and development

Every staff member completes mandatory induction and role-specific training before working unsupervised, tracked through the Mandatory Training Matrix.

Health and safety responsibilities

Every staff member has a personal responsibility to work safely, follow the Health and Safety Policy Full Manual, and report a hazard or concern promptly.

Right to work and DBS checks

Every staff member's right to work in the UK is verified before their first day per the Right to Work Checks Procedure, and a role involving regulated activity requires an enhanced DBS check, renewed on the cycle set out in the DBS Renewal Procedure.

Lone working and personal safety

A staff member whose role involves lone working is issued the equipment and follows the process set out in the Lone Worker Devices Policy.

Expenses and travel

A genuine, reasonable work expense, including mileage for an approved journey, is reimbursed per the Staff Expenses Policy.

IT and communication systems

Every staff member with a login to an Alderbridge system follows the Password and Account Access Guidance, and any issued device is covered by the Mobile Device Management Policy.

Supervision and appraisal

Every staff member receives regular one-to-one supervision with their line manager, and an Annual Performance and Development Review, per the Staff Supervision and Appraisal Policy.

Leaving Alderbridge

A staff member resigning gives notice per the table above, returns any issued equipment, key or access card, and receives a final payslip reflecting any outstanding holiday pay.

Grievance and whistleblowing routes

A staff member with a workplace concern uses the Grievance Procedure for a personal employment matter, or the Whistleblowing Policy where the concern relates to a wider wrongdoing or risk, including an anonymous route where preferred.

Safeguarding responsibilities

Every staff member, regardless of role, has a personal responsibility to recognise and report a safeguarding concern immediately per the Adult Safeguarding Policy and the wider safeguarding suite, a responsibility that sits above any other single term of employment given what is genuinely at stake for a resident.

answer_parts.text: For three years' service the handbook's notice table applies: for 2 years or more the required notice is one week per completed year, so after three years you give three weeks' notice.

When you resign you should give notice as above, and complete the usual leaving steps: return any issued equipment, keys or access cards; HR will run the exit process including a final pay calculation and (where you agree) an exit interview; and you will receive a final payslip that reflects any outstanding holiday pay.
